decisions.reason: As a newly launched resin injection unit that fits closely with the firm's core application-equipment business, it is likely to be retained while management waits for clearer performance evidence and uses its moderate organisational slack.

Although another new resin injection unit may face internal comparison with A and with existing aspirations, its strong strategic fit and the firm's established engineering-sales system make continued market presence more likely than withdrawal after only one year.

An automatic airless spray gun sits squarely in the firm's established product domain, so absent clear signs of underperformance, behavioral-theory logic suggests keeping it because results are still being learned and no urgent problemistic search is triggered.

The manual airless spray gun is a core-type product for this firm and German industrial customers value reliability and continuity, so management would likely keep it unless early sales clearly fell below aspiration levels.

The air-assisted airless spray gun extends a familiar technology platform and supports the firm's customization strategy, which makes retention likely while the firm assesses acceptance across different industrial uses.

The data logger is somewhat more experimental than the hardware launches, so its uncertainty raises the chance of exit, but it still supports the firm's stated move toward innovative application technology and would likely be kept for another year.
